post.description: Runs a script on one of the branch's Postgres databases on a fresh connection as the database's owner (or, with `role`, after `SET ROLE` to it: a preview of that role's view, not a security boundary). The script is sent unchanged as one simple query, so multi-statement scripts, explicit transactions and commands like `VACUUM` work. Unless `confirm` is true, risky statements (drops, truncates, `DELETE`/`UPDATE` without `WHERE`, also under `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` or `PREPARE`, and anything that doesn't parse) and, on a protected branch, every statement that isn't a read are held back with 409 `sql_confirm_required`. Errors before the connection opens are JSON; then the answer is `200 application/x-ndjson`, one JSON event per line: `notice`, `columns` (`statement`, `columns: [{name, type}]`), `rows` (`statement`, at most 200 rows of text-or-null values), `complete` (`statement`, `tag`, `rows`, `truncated`: over 1,000 rows), `error` (`statement`, `code`, `message`, `detail`, `hint`, `position`: 1-based in the sent text), `heartbeat` (after 15 s without another event) and, always last, `done` (`outcome`: `ok`, `error`, `cancelled`, `timeout` or `truncated_response` past 10 MiB; `duration_ms`). Closing the stream cancels the run. Every run is logged with its command tags and a SHA-256 of the script, never the script.

schema.description: `^[a-z_][a-z0-9_]{0,62}$`, default `public`; not a reserved schema. Fixed once enabled.

RestoreAccepted.description:
The 202 body of a restore: the branch is `resetting`, and its previous state is kept as a
backup branch.

backup_branch_id.description: The backup branch holding the state before the restore.

at.description: The point in the branch's history to rewind to.

RoleInUseKey.description: A data API key that names an owner-level role; also the `keys` extra of `role_in_use`.

RoleLevel.description:
What a role may do: `OwnerLevel` is the wide definition (superuser, CREATEROLE, CREATEDB,
BYPASSRLS, REPLICATION, or `neon_superuser` at any depth).

RoleOrigin.description:
Where a `neon_roles` row came from: the branch's owner, a role made in SQL, or one made
through the API.

confirm.description: `true` runs statements the guard would hold back.

database.description: The Postgres database; null or absent is the branch's main database.

role.description: The role to `SET ROLE` to first; null or absent runs as the owner.

run_id.description: Chosen by the client; names the run for `…/sql/runs/{run_id}/cancel`.

sql.description: The script, sent as one simple query: 1 byte to 1 MiB.

SchemaEntry.description: One schema's tables, functions (overloads by name) and enums (labels by name).

TableDesc.description: A table, view or foreign table. `privileges` (role to held privileges) is `null` unless asked for.

primary_key.description:
The primary key's columns, in the key's order; left out when there is none (a view,
or a table without a key).

email.description: A new address, verified unless `email_verified` is false.

email_verified.description:
With `email`, whether the new address is verified (default true); alone, sets the flag
on the current address (false sends the user a verification code).

password.description: A new password; the user's sessions end.

protected.description:
`true` refuses deleting the branch, resetting it to its parent and deleting its
database; restore still works.

UpdateDatabaseRequest.description: All optional; a missing one is left as it is. `history_window` is in seconds.

UpdateKeyRequest.description:
Which databases a key may reach. `databases` has no default, so an empty body can't widen a
key to every database by accident.

databases.description:
The Postgres databases the key may reach (1 to 20 databases of the branch, disabled ones
included), or null for every served database. Required.

default_schema.description: The schema a request to this database uses when it names none: `^[a-z_][a-z0-9_]{0,62}$`.

grant_existing.description:
Also grant the data API roles on the objects already in the schema (default false).
Without it, only objects created from now on get grants (through default privileges),
plus, once per database, the first schema's existing objects (a database whose first
enable ran while its schema was missing gets that full first grant once the schema
exists, flag or not). Grants only: it never revokes anything. Sent with an unchanged
`default_schema` it grants on that schema's existing objects now, and answers 409
`data_api_disabled` when the database isn't served.

pg_database.description: `null` or `""` clears the hint; absent leaves it.

role.description: `null` or `""` clears the hint; absent leaves it.

version.description: The version the client last saw; a mismatch answers 409 `saved_query_conflict`.
